stem: What should you choose before testing a device?
choices: A different device for every trial
why: An evaluation begins with what to do and how success will be judged.
evidence: First choose a task and success criteria

stem: Which record is useful evidence for a short text test?
choices: Someone said all devices are fast.
The edited sentence and button feedback appeared in each of three trials.
why: Specific observations from repeated trials support a judgment.

stem: The short text test succeeds. Which limit belongs in the report?
choices: Long video editing was not tested.
This proves every possible task works.
No limits need to be reported.
why: Conclusions stay within the task tested.

stem: Which pairing correctly identifies hardware and software?
why: Physical parts are hardware; the editor supplies instructions.

stem: The task is recording an audio message. Which fictional combination meets all requirements?
why: B supplies the working microphone and Voice Pad records audio.
evidence: B + Voice Pad is the only pairing

stem: For a typed announcement with a lower-battery goal, which recommendation uses the supplied facts?
choices: A + Text Pad: both text pairings work, and A uses less battery for text.
B + Voice Pad: text editing does not matter.
A + Voice Pad: a microphone is not needed for editing.
why: The choice meets the text requirements and then applies the battery criterion.
evidence: A uses less battery for text

stem: In the paused-editor case, what is the observed symptom?
choices: No sentence appears after Send sample.
why: The symptom is the missing output; pause is the cause in this simulation.

stem: Why test one possible cause at a time?
choices: To change as many things as possible.
To connect a change with its result.
why: One-change tests help show which change helped.
evidence: you cannot tell which one helped

stem: Pause is on and Wi-Fi is connected. Which solution is best supported and safest?
choices: Resume practice typing, then send the sample again.
why: Resuming addresses the evidence; repeating the task verifies the fix.
evidence: Resume practice typing is an evidence-supported, reversible solution

stem: Which help message gives enough information to follow the solution?
choices: No text appeared; Wi-Fi was connected and pause was on; I resumed and resent; text appeared.
why: It includes the symptom, checks and results, solution, and verification.
evidence: symptom, tests and results, solution and reason, and the final check
